purpose: Bounded adapter contract for nested orchestrators. A provider is listed only with the evidence that it exists; nothing here installs, downloads or upgrades a provider, and EOS never runs a nested task it cannot bound.

policy.missing_runtime: ADAPTER_ONLY -- the contract is known, nothing is executed, and the caller is told which capability is unavailable
policy.discovery: a skill package that ships orchestrator.contract.json declares itself; a name alone is never a capability
policy.bounds: every provider must declare timeout_seconds, max_depth and max_agents; max_steps bounds total worker executions; a probe is a bounded version call, never a task
policy.execution: a probe is not delegation. `orchestrators run` executes only when the contract names execution.protocol=eos-orchestrator/1; a provider without that contract stays ADAPTER_ONLY even when its binary answers --version
policy.permissions: write, network, execute and outside_workspace are booleans so a caller can refuse before delegating
policy.evidence: a provider that runs must have an evidence directory and a format for what it returns

classes.INSTRUCTION: prose guidance only; no execution surface
classes.TOOL_PROVIDER: ships tools, usually MCP, but no agents
classes.WORKFLOW_PROVIDER: runs a declared pipeline of steps

execution.note: Ruflo exposes MCP tools, not the EOS json-stdin worker boundary. Until an adapter implements eos-orchestrator/1, a version probe must not be reported as a successful delegation.

delegation.note: the specialist inventory is read from the provider at run time; EOS does not cache a roster it cannot verify

side_effects: may install dependencies into the project
writes provider state under the project or the home directory
spawns child agent sessions outside the host's own loop

cost.billing: delegated to the host model provider
cost.budget: bounded by the EOS timeout and max_agents, not by the provider
